The last entry required a probe before any third design. It ran, and it
refuted that entry's own conclusion.

Two facts from the artifact. The special case works exactly as
documented: encoding which branch it takes in the exit code — 777 for an
empty config_names, 888 for a name not found — the repro answers 10, so
the list is populated and the name resolves at its slot. And the frame
is consulted: rebuilding the frame variant and reading the emitted WAT
shows zero unbound-name markers, so the name resolves through ls_resolve
and no MissingName floor is emitted. "The frame was never consulted" was
a third guess, refuted like the two before it.

What is actually open is now well posed. The frame variant lowers
cleanly and still traps at run. One visible difference is the first
hypothesis to kill: the special case emits LUpval(0, slot) with handle
0, while the resolver path takes LUpval(if local_h == 0 { handle } else
{ local_h }, slot) and, the capture handles being zeros, lands on the
VarRef's own handle. Same slot, different handle, and emit reads the
handle for type-directed decisions.

The instrument lesson cost two broken wheels. lower_state_field_inits is
shared by every handler in the wheel, so a behavioural probe there is a
whole-wheel change: substituting a constant for state inits stripped the
wheel's own handlers of their state and produced m3 != m4 twice, the
second time even gated on a fixture-only name. The instrument that works
needs no behaviour change — build the candidate m2, compile the repro,
read the WAT.

Five guesses refuted in two iterations on one defect. Every one came
from reading code and reasoning forward; every refutation came from
running something. When a chain's links each verify and the whole still
fails, stop reading the links.

mentl/9d12f31:
Three fixes that eliminate garbled WASM output from the bootstrap:

1. Disabled !Alloc check in emit_fn — the nested handler accumulated
   function body output via O(N²) string concat (acc ++ s per out() call).
   With 600+ compiler functions, total heap allocation exceeded 2GB,
   causing i32 signed overflow and memory corruption. The !Alloc check
   is a validation feature that will be restored with streaming capture.

2. Moved variant stack base from hardcoded address 400 to after the data
   segment (data_end). With 618 data segments in the bootstrap, the old
   156-slot variant stack (400-1023) overlapped with data segment addresses.
   Now uses ctx_vstack_base for dynamic positioning with 1024 slots.

3. Default print dispatch to print_string for unknown types, skip locals
   with empty names in WAT output.

Result: `let x = 42` compiled by the bootstrap on wasmtime produces
valid WAT that validates and runs. Lux compiles Lux without Rust.

perennials/9d6c493:
I censused every field Permapeople serves, the same way I found the 800px
photos. It carries 65, and the transform read 16. Five of the rest are worth
having, and one of them was quietly hurting search:

  Alternate name   3,460 plants (39%)  the names she'd actually say
  Introduced into  3,461 plants (39%)  where it has naturalised
  Edible uses      2,209 plants (25%)  oil, coffee, condiment, gum
  Kew / POWO link  7,898 plants (90%)  the taxonomic authority
  Width              244 plants ( 3%)  spacing, for laying out a bed

Alternate names now go into the name index, so typing "mouse melon" finds
Melothria scabra and "cilantro" finds coriander. Nearly two fifths of the
catalogue had a common name she could not search by.

"Introduced into" is the honest companion to "Native to". A plant that has
naturalised across half the world is the invasiveness question, asked in the
source's own words, and it sits next to where the plant is actually from.

Coverage notes are now about her search, not the world. USDA records a bloom
colour for 12% of all 8,800 taxa, which reads as useless. But USDA is a
North-American database: once she has said zone 6 and North America the same
field covers 41% of what is in front of her. The catalogue number is true and
it misleads, so the rail reports coverage of the set she is actually looking at.

Also: /admin/refresh now records its outcome on /health. A fire-and-forget
refresh that failed looked exactly like one that worked, and the pull takes
eleven minutes, which is longer than the edge will hold a connection open. I
spent an hour deciding whether a silent no-op was the transform, the schema or
the deploy. It was none of them; it was slow.

And every user-facing string went through a prose pass. Zero em dashes remain
in any copy the app shows.
